edits.before: Levels 4-6 are Sett's grit window and you have to respect it. His passive double-punch and grit-charged W mean he out-trades you in any sustained exchange your spirit healing can't keep up with — your poke chips him, but the damage you eat in trades fuels the W that one-shots your follow-up. At 6 you finally get a tool: drop R (Between Worlds) and the spirit-realm untargetability blanks his R suppress-slam and lets you walk out of a pull he commits. Bait the E pull, R through it, then Q-burst — but if he holds the pull, hold your all-in. Don't duel him straight; you lose the grit war.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are Sett's grit window and you have to respect it. His passive double-punch and grit-charged Haymaker mean he out-trades you in any sustained exchange your spirit healing cannot keep up with, and the centre of that smash is true damage, so MR does nothing about it. At 6 you finally get a tool: Between Worlds gives you a two-way teleport across the rift that he has no way to copy. Bait Facebreaker on its 16s cooldown, cross the rift while it is down, then Q-burst. What you must not do is hold the rift until he presses The Show Stopper — it grounds, and grounding locks out Across the Veil and Between Worlds together.

edits.before: Past two items this stays a knife-fight, not a free win. Sett's bruiser scaling and grit-charged W still threaten to delete you the moment his E pull lands and your W is down — you are a squishy mage with one leap. Your edge is the W-reset snowball: catch him with R untargetability in a skirmish, land Q burst, and your W refreshes off the takedown to peel out. Don't facecheck for a pull, never trade into a full grit W, and look to pick him in the side lane with vision rather than brawl him head-on. If you fell behind early, scale with your team and let your poke matter in fights, not 1v1.
edits.after: Past two items this stays a knife-fight, not a free win. Sett's bruiser scaling and grit-charged Haymaker still threaten to delete you the moment Facebreaker lands and your W is down — you are a squishy mage with one leap. Your edge is the W-reset snowball: catch him with a rift crossing in a skirmish, land Q burst, and your W refreshes off the takedown to peel out. Never facecheck for a pull, never trade into a full grit Haymaker, and never let The Show Stopper catch you holding a movement spell — its grounding locks both of yours. Pick him in the side lane with vision instead of brawling him head-on.

notes:
THE BIG ONE: five strings in this entry give Aurora 'spirit-realm untargetability' on Between Worlds. She has no untargetability anywhere in her kit — Across the Veil grants invisibility and Between Worlds grants a two-way teleport. This is the same class of fabrication as the Cassiopeia and Brand calibration cases, but worse, because it tells the reader to hold a 120-second ultimate for a suppression dodge that does not exist. I fixed every reachable instance; the phrase may well appear in other Aurora matchups and is worth a repo-wide grep for 'untargetab' in champ-data/content/aurora.js.

The suspectName 'Show Stopper' was a REAL hit — Riot's name is The Show Stopper.

The Show Stopper GROUNDS (kit flag plus _missing dash-denied). Nothing in the entry said so. Grounding is the single most important fact in this matchup for a champion whose entire defence is two dashes.

'Between the Worlds' (extra 'the') appears again in the full layer.

full.focus.text is 'Sett Haymaker' with letters ['W']. I would argue for 'Sett Facebreaker' / ['E'] since the pull gates everything, but that is a judgement call about what the loading screen should teach, so I left it and am flagging it rather than deciding for you.

Deliberately not asserted: whether Aurora can Flash-buffer out of a Show Stopper grounding, and whether Tenacity shortens the suppression. aurora.json needsResearch is empty on both and I will not infer them.
